items.name: Wilson measure

items.statement:
For an integer $s\ge1$ and $\beta\in\R$, put $\Lambda_s=(\Z/s\Z)^4$. A configuration assigns $U(y,a)\in G$ to every positive link, with inverse on the reversed link. Define
\begin{align*}
U_{y;ab}&=U(y,a)U(y+e_a,b)U(y+e_b,a)^{-1}U(y,b)^{-1},\\
E_s^{\rm W}(U)&=\sum_{y\in\Lambda_s}\sum_{a<b}\wilsonterm(U_{y;ab}),\\
d\mu_{s,\beta}(U)&=Z_{s,\beta}^{-1}e^{-\beta E_s^{\rm W}(U)}\prod_{y,a}dh(U(y,a))\,.
\end{align*}
Here $dh$ is probability Haar measure and $Z_{s,\beta}$ normalizes the measure. This is the lattice theory to be scaled.

items.name: Existence

items.name: Nontriviality
items.label: rem:nontriviality
items.statement:
Q3 requires a nonzero smeared field, as in the formal statement; given faithfulness and the covering clause, this is equivalent to $\mathcal L
e0$, and in the construction it is met by the unit field (Step~ef{step:deduction-hierarchy}). Nontriviality comes from the trace: $\Theta
e0$ (Theorem~ef{prop:TR}), so faithfulness gives $\Phi(\iota_4\Theta,f)
e0$ for some~$f$, while its vacuum expectation vanishes; hence it is not a multiple of the identity. Q6 gives a positive limit $\lim_{r\downarrow0}r^8\log^2(1/r)	racetwopoint(r)=3\dimG/\pi^4$ and excludes equality with every finite Wick profile on any interval~$(0,\delta)$. Thus every Gaussian or finite free-field realization whose two-point profile for~$\Theta$ belongs to the class of Definition~ef{def:D17} is excluded.

items.name: Construction
items.label: thm:B
items.statement:
For every gauge group~$G$ of Definition~\ref{def:D01} and~$\blockpenalty>0$, the renormalized insertions (Definition~\ref{def:D08}) on the penalty-$\blockpenalty$ trajectories of Theorem~\ref{prop:MT} form a regular Wilson family~$\mathcal W$ with $a_N\downarrow0$, $L_p\uparrow\infty$ and $\beta_{N,p}/\log(1/a_N)\to\slope$ uniformly in~$p$. Moreover:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},nosep]
\item For every~$p$, token list~$v$ and $p$-admissible separated~$f$, $\latsmear_{N,p}(v;f)\to\int fM^{\rm UV}_{p,v}$ as $N\to\infty$.
\item For every strictly increasing~$\mathsf p$ there are a strictly increasing~$\mathsf q$, a table~$S$ satisfying E1--E7 and hierarchy data over~$\mathcal W$ satisfying Q2--Q6 with $\mathcal W\to S$ and $\mathcal W\to S^{\rm mix}\circ\pi_{\rm quo}$ along~$P=\mathsf p\circ\mathsf q$. In (iii)--(v), $S$ is this table, $F_d=V_d/\nullspace{d}(S)$, and $\nu$, $\xi_*$, $\Theta$ are those of these hierarchy data.
\item $S=\int_{\phases}S^\xi\,d\nu(\xi)$ with $\nu$ a fully supported probability measure on a compact metric space; each~$S^\xi$ continues a faithful Wightman theory with unique vacuum.
\item A conserved stress tensor is normalized by its shell fluxes (Theorem~\ref{prop:ST}); in the selected phase~$\xi_*$ its centered trace~$\Theta$ has $r^8\log^2(1/r)\tracetwopoint(r)\to3\dimG/\pi^4$, and $\tracetwopoint$ agrees with no finite Wick profile on any interval~$(0,\delta)$.
\item The fields~$F_d$ have an operator product expansion with spectator-independent coefficients and $|\mathcal R_D^\zeta|\le r^{D+1-|\boldsymbol A|_{\deg}-\varepsilon}$, with the quantifiers and uniformity of Theorem~\ref{prop:OP}, and contact extensions from the same prescription.
\end{enumerate}

items.name: Further results
items.statement:
Further conclusions about these same objects are proved in Part~II: Lemma~\ref{lem:E1.3} gives endpoint tuning, Lemma~\ref{lem:E3.2} gives convergence at moving points, and Lemma~\ref{lem:H2.3} gives low-energy bounds. The spectral results are cited in Step~\ref{step:deduction-trace}; the nested product results are cited below. The position-space two-point scaling consequence is given after Lemma~\ref{lem:I1.3}.

Lemmas~\ref{lem:I2.2}, \ref{lem:I2.3} and~\ref{lem:I2.4} give further polynomial and Fock countertests in the same selected phase.

Lemmas~\ref{lem:J1.3}--\ref{lem:J1.6} give further integrated and nested estimates for this prescription.

With~$j_q=\jmath_{q,q+1}$, set

\delta_q^{\rm pres}&=\min_{0\le d\le q}a_d^{\rm ct}\,.
\end{align*}
These give the graded contact subtractions and their common range of separated evaluation.
